name: Inside the Atom: From Rays in the Dark to the Chain Reaction
description: The physicists who found X-rays, radioactivity, the electron, the nucleus and the neutron, built quantum mechanics, and in 1938 and 1939 learned that the uranium atom could be split.

checkpoints.name: Rays and electrons
checkpoints.note: The discovery of X-rays in 1895 and of radioactivity by Becquerel in 1896 opens the hunt. The Curies find new elements, Thomson finds the electron in 1897, Planck introduces the quantum, Einstein's special relativity links mass and energy, and Rutherford finds the atomic nucleus in 1911.

checkpoints.name: The quantum atom
checkpoints.note: The Bohr model puts electrons in fixed orbits, and Heisenberg, Schrodinger and Dirac turn it into quantum mechanics. The Geiger counter clicks for each particle, Chadwick finds the neutron in 1932, the cyclotron smashes atoms, Szilard imagines a chain reaction, and Fermi shows that neutrons can make atoms radioactive.

checkpoints.name: Fission
checkpoints.note: In December 1938 Hahn and Strassmann find barium after firing neutrons at uranium, and Lise Meitner explains it as nuclear fission. In 1939 Szilard and Fermi show that fission frees more neutrons, so a chain reaction is possible, and Szilard and Einstein warn the American president.
